question: An 82-year-old man with alcohol use disorder is brought to the emergency department from his assisted living facility because of fever and cough for 1 week. The cough is productive of thick, mucoid, blood-tinged sputum. His temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F) and respirations are 20/min. Physical examination shows coarse inspiratory crackles over the right lung field. Sputum cultures grow gram-negative, encapsulated bacilli that are resistant to amoxicillin, ceftriaxone, and aztreonam. Which of the following infection control measures is most appropriate for preventing transmission of this organism to other patients in the hospital?

options.opa: Require all staff and visitors to wear droplet masks
options.opb: Transfer patient to a positive pressure room
options.opc: Require autoclave sterilization of all medical instruments
options.opd: Isolate patient to a single-occupancy room
options.ope: Transfer patient to a negative pressure room

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "82-year-old man with alcohol use disorder" -> "fever and cough for 1 week" -> "productive of thick, mucoid, blood-tinged sputum" -> "temperature 38.5°C, respirations 20/min" -> "coarse inspiratory crackles over right lung field" -> "sputum cultures grow gram-negative, encapsulated bacilli resistant to multiple antibiotics" -> "infection control measures required" -> 80%
enhanced_information: For preventing transmission of gram-negative, encapsulated bacilli resistant to multiple antibiotics from an 82-year-old man with alcohol use disorder, isolating the patient to a single-occupancy room is the most appropriate infection control measure. This is based on the patient's clinical presentation and the resistance pattern of the organism, which indicates the need for strict isolation to prevent spread to other patients.
analysis: The core medical principle here is to prevent transmission of a multi-drug resistant gram-negative organism from an elderly patient with alcohol use disorder. Given the patient's clinical presentation and resistance pattern, the most appropriate infection control measure is to isolate the patient to a single-occupancy room to prevent spread to other patients.
